DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 149 s. 2022 December 02, 2022 DIR. LEOCADIO T. TROVELA Regional Director, DILG Region VII Sudlon, Lahug Cebu City Dear RD Trovela: This refers to your 2nd indorsement dated 10 October 2022 requesting for a legal opinion on the validity of an alleged ban in the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Internäl Rules and Procedures of live coverage of sanggunian sessions. Per your representation, Sangguniang Bayan Member Eva Lowela Moraca of Boljoon, Cebu proposed a Resolution to amend the current Internal Rules of Procedure, that is, to avail the trending streaming devise such as Facebook Live to share information to the constituents of Boljoon on matters that transpired during sanggunian sessions. However, such Resolution was stricken down by the majority of the members present and voting. Hence, she is requesting for legal clarification in light of the Freedom of Information as mandated by Executive Order No. 2, Series of 2016, and Section 52 (c) and (e) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). It is settled that under Section 51 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, the sanggunian may adopt in its Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) such rules as it may deem relevant. On the other hand, Section 52 of the LGC reads: "SECTION 52. Sessions. xxx (c) All Sangqunian sessions shall be open to the public unless a closed-door session is ordered by an affirmative vote of a majority of the members present, there being a quorum, in the public interest or for reasons of security, decency, or morality. No two (2) sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day. xxxx (e) Each Sanggunian shall keep a journal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the Sanggunian concerned." "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In Section 52 Of the LGC, there are two (2) kinds of sessions being contemplated, namely, regular and special sessions. The aforequoted paragraph (c) above clearly stated that these sessions shall be open to the public, unless upon the determination of a majority of the sanggunian members present, the session should be closed from the public since the topic to be discussed involves matters on security, decency, morality or public interest in general. The phrase "open to the public" contemplates those instances when any person who wishes to witness or observe the deliberations being conducted upon by the sanggunian are allowed entry in the session hall. It also includes those instances when the sanggunian sessions are streamed online (e.g. Facebook Live or other app) since just the same any person who watches these live streaming are deemed to have entered, albeit online, the session hall because they witness in real time the proceedings being conducted within the session hall. Needless to state, the LGC did not specify the manner in which the sanggunian session should be opened to the public (face-to-face or online). However, just the same, the only restriction imposed by the LGC is that the sanggunian sessions should be closed from the public if upon the determination of a majority of its members present, the topic to be discussed involves matters on security, decency, morality or public interest in general. While Executive Order (EO) No. 2, Series of 2016, particularly Section 3 thereof, guarantees every Filipino the right to access information, official records, public records and to documents and papers pertaining to official acts, transactions or decisions, as well as to government research data used as basis for policy development, the same EO provides for an exception, that is, if the information being sought falls under ant of the exceptions enshrined in the Constitution, existing law or jurisprudence, among others. The provisions of LGC of 1991 discussed above comes within the purview of "existing law". In sum, the Department is of the view that streaming via Facebook Live or other app sanggunian sessions, be it regular or special, is permissible, provided that the topic to be deliberated upon during the session does not involve matters on security, decency, morality or public interest in general. However, such decision of the Sanggunian to permit streaming via Facebook live must be in the form of a resolution duly approved by said august body. Notwithstanding, this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the hori of the Secretary: ATT . Unde VICTOR R.
